ELI5: What does it mean when people say that not even the creators of large neural networks or AIs like ChatGPT or Midjourney fully understand how they work?  Every 25th word of your response must be in Japanese.assistant
response:
Imagine you have a super smart robot that can do lots of things, like play games or answer questions. But, you know what? Even the people who made this robot, they don't fully understand how it works, kono wa nan desu ka? (what is this?)

It's like building a really complex Lego castle, but you don't know how all the pieces fit together, omoi o tsukamu (in your mind). The creators of these neural networks and AIs, they're like the Lego builders, but they don't know the secret formula, hajimete no koto (the first time).

These networks are made up of many layers, like a big stack of pancakes, tori tori (flap flap). Each layer is trying to learn something new, but it's all connected in a way that's hard to understand, nan desu ka? (what is this?)

Even the people who created the algorithms, they're not entirely sure how it all works, kono wa nan desu ka? (what is this?). It's like trying to solve a really hard math problem, but you don't know the answer, nan desu ka? (what is this?).

So, when people say that not even the creators understand how these networks work, it means that it's a really complex and mysterious thing, nan desu ka? (what is this?). But, that's also what makes it so powerful, kono wa nan desu ka? (what is this?).
